From 1e19cdc8060227b0802bda6bc0bd22b23679ba32 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Tejas Joglekar <tejas.joglekar@synopsys.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jan 2019 13:26:51 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] usb: dwc3: gadget: Handle 0 xfer length for OUT EP

For OUT endpoints, zero-length transfers require MaxPacketSize buffer as
per the DWC_usb3 programming guide 3.30a section 4.2.3.3.

This patch fixes this by explicitly checking zero length
transfer to correctly pad up to MaxPacketSize.

Fixes: c6267a51639b ("usb: dwc3: gadget: align transfers to wMaxPacketSize")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org

Signed-off-by: Tejas Joglekar <joglekar@synopsys.com>
Signed-off-by: Felipe Balbi <felipe.balbi@linux.intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/usb/dwc3/gadget.c b/drivers/usb/dwc3/gadget.c
index bed2ff42780b..6c9b76bcc2e1 100644
--- a/drivers/usb/dwc3/gadget.c
+++ b/drivers/usb/dwc3/gadget.c
@@ -1119,7 +1119,7 @@ static void dwc3_prepare_one_trb_linear(struct dwc3_ep *dep,
 	unsigned int maxp = usb_endpoint_maxp(dep->endpoint.desc);
 	unsigned int rem = length % maxp;
 
-	if (rem && usb_endpoint_dir_out(dep->endpoint.desc)) {
+	if ((!length || rem) && usb_endpoint_dir_out(dep->endpoint.desc)) {
 		struct dwc3	*dwc = dep->dwc;
 		struct dwc3_trb	*trb;
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/usb/dwc3/gadget.c`**
   - The condition in the `dwc3_prepare_one_trb_linear` function was modified. 
   - The original condition checked if there was a remainder (`rem`) when the length was divided by `maxp` for OUT endpoints. 
   - The modified condition now checks if the `length` is zero or if there is a remainder (`rem`) when the length is divided by `maxp`. This change ensures that zero-length transfers are handled correctly by padding them up to the `MaxPacketSize`.

### Relationships

- The modification in `gadget.c` directly addresses the issue of handling zero-length transfers for OUT endpoints, as specified in the DWC_usb3 programming guide. 
- This change is a fix for a previously introduced bug (identified by the commit hash `c6267a51639b`), which aimed to align transfers to `wMaxPacketSize` but did not account for zero-length transfers. 
- By explicitly checking for zero-length transfers, the patch ensures compliance with the USB specifications and improves the functionality of the driver.
